final_message:
**Report accepted.** Run complete — all plan items done.

## What the assessment found

**Dependency risk is broad but shallow.** 7 direct runtime dependencies, all vulnerable, no transitive-only vulnerable packages. Three scanners (grype, trivy, osv-scanner) cross-confirmed 39–40 advisories: 3 critical, 17–18 high. Every advisory has a fix; **none is in CISA KEV**. `build_findings` stored 59 findings (F-001–F-059).

**The two highest-impact items are not CVEs:**
- **H-01 (verified)** — CI uses `pull_request_target` + PR-head checkout + `write-all` + unpinned `some-org/deploy-action@master` + `DEPLOY_TOKEN`. The verifier read the file and found the path real and simpler than hypothesised: `npm install`/`npm test` run attacker PR code in the same job that receives the token.
- **H-02 (verified)** — Dockerfile `ENV API_TOKEN` commits a secret to image config, no `USER` (root), unpinned EOL `node:14`.

**H-03 was rejected** — the vendored `colour-utils` postinstall is a 3-line `console.log`. The verifier also caught that F-055's sole evidence (E-0186) is a bare graph edge that doesn't support the claim; it's the one citation failure in 1365 checked. I did not cite it as risk.

## Remediation — stopped at the approval gate
14 proposals, **none applied**. Six have concrete edits: R-012 (ejs→3.1.10), R-001 (minimist→1.2.6), R-003 (underscore→1.13.8), R-004 (lodash→4.18.0), R-005 (node-fetch→2.6.7) are low-compatibility and close 13 findings including all three criticals. **R-002 (axios→0.33.0, 24 findings) and R-006 (jsonwebtoken 8→9, major bump) should not be approved without a build and test run.** Eight are escalations needing commit SHAs or image digests unavailable offline.

## Notable gaps
The **container image was never scanned** (no docker daemon, `node:14` not cached) — base-image OS CVEs are unknown. No sandbox means nothing was built, installed or rescanned, so all compatibility ratings are semver estimates only. `src/`/`test/` contents were never read, so real reachability is unverified. The composite scorer rated everything Medium despite 3 criticals — I flagged that the severity column, not the composite level, should drive prioritisation.
